subject.title: memory flush never triggers when reserveTokensFloor equals contextWindow

question: Should memory flush use the same context-window-capped effective reserve budget as embedded compaction, or should oversized `reserveTokensFloor` be treated as invalid config that requires a doctor/config repair?
rationale: Current source proves the bug path, but competing prior fixes and compatibility labels show that changing this threshold alters existing session flush timing.

options.title: Reuse effective reserve budget
options.body: Route memory flush and preflight gates through the same capped reserve calculation used by embedded compaction, with tests for oversized floors and normal large-window behavior.

options.title: Doctor-repair invalid floors
options.body: Keep runtime strict and add a doctor/config repair path that rewrites `reserveTokensFloor >= contextWindowTokens` before runtime gates consume it.

options.title: Defer to adaptive threshold work
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/81417 or a successor settle broader memory-flush threshold policy before fixing this narrow edge case.

recommendation.title: Reuse effective reserve budget
recommendation.body: Route memory flush and preflight gates through the same capped reserve calculation used by embedded compaction, with tests for oversized floors and normal large-window behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected feature history and prior review routing most directly point to this handle for memory-flush budget policy.
